title: The conjugate isomorphism in a square of adjunctions
statement:
Consider four adjunctions

$$
E_1\dashv\mathrm{Res}_1\colon\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B,\quad
E_2\dashv\mathrm{Res}_2\colon\mathcal A'\rightleftarrows\mathcal B',\quad
U_1\dashv L_1\colon\mathcal A'\rightleftarrows\mathcal A,\quad
U_2\dashv L_2\colon\mathcal B'\rightleftarrows\mathcal B
$$

(left adjoints $E_1\colon\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $E_2\colon\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$,
$U_1\colon\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$, $U_2\colon\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$), and a natural
isomorphism $e\colon\mathrm{Res}_2\circ L_2\cong L_1\circ\mathrm{Res}_1$ of functors
$\mathcal B\to\mathcal A'$ between the composites of right adjoints. The *conjugate* of $e$ is
the natural isomorphism

$$
E_1\circ U_1\;\cong\;U_2\circ E_2\colon\mathcal A'\longrightarrow\mathcal B
$$

corresponding to $e$ under the bijection between natural transformations of left adjoints and
of right adjoints for the composite adjunctions $E_1U_1\dashv L_1\mathrm{Res}_1$ and
$U_2E_2\dashv\mathrm{Res}_2L_2$.

mathlib_searches.query: conjugate isomorphism from an isomorphism between composites of right adjoints
conjugate isomorphism between composites of right adjoints gives isomorphism between composites of left adjoints
A natural isomorphism between right adjoint functors induces a canonical isomorphism of their left adjoints by conjugation
mathlib_searches.verdict: match: conjugateIsoEquiv is the canonical conjugation equivalence; the alternative natIsoOfRightAdjointNatIso is deprecated (Opposites.lean:93–100).
no match: Loogle reports an unknown identifier; the declaration is present in the pinned local Mathlib source but deprecated.
match: source locations for Adjunction.comp (Basic.lean:567) and conjugateIsoEquiv (Mates.lean:425), with the declaration bodies read independently.

mathlib_searches.query: Uniqueness of left adjoints under a natural isomorphism of right adjoint functors, using the mate correspondence
mathlib_searches.verdict: related: leftAdjointUniq and its unit/counit equations concern a common right adjoint; conjugateIsoEquiv handles the supplied isomorphism directly.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: write adj₁ : E₁ ⊣ Res₁, adj₂ : E₂ ⊣ Res₂, adjR : U₁ ⊣ L₁ and adjS : U₂ ⊣ L₂ for the four given adjunctions. Then `(CategoryTheory.conjugateIsoEquiv (adj₂.comp adjS) (adjR.comp adj₁)).symm e : U₁ ⋙ E₁ ≅ E₂ ⋙ U₂`, where `e : L₂ ⋙ Res₂ ≅ Res₁ ⋙ L₁`. CategoryTheory.Adjunction.comp (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Basic.lean:562–573, definition at 567) supplies the first pair E₂ ⋙ U₂ ⊣ L₂ ⋙ Res₂ and the second pair U₁ ⋙ E₁ ⊣ Res₁ ⋙ L₁. CategoryTheory.conjugateIsoEquiv (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean:385–389, 425–435) therefore has type (U₁ ⋙ E₁ ≅ E₂ ⋙ U₂) ≃ (L₂ ⋙ Res₂ ≅ Res₁ ⋙ L₁); its inverse at e is the required canonical conjugate, with hom and inv defined at lines 430–433 by conjugateEquiv.symm on e.hom and, with adjunctions interchanged, e.inv.
